description:
Hi, I'm David, CEO and co-founder of Whippy. I'm hiring a Quantitative Marketing Manager to own the story of what Whippy is worth to a staffing company, prove it with numbers, and turn it into deals, retention, and upsells.

Why I'm hiring

Whippy is bootstrapped, profitable, and the category leader in AI communication for staffing, with over 1,000 customers and new industries opening behind it. Today, a lot of our marketing still comes from me. I wrote our case studies and I host our webinars. That got us here. It does not scale, and it is not where my time should go.

The thesis for this role is simple. Learn our customers better than anyone. Put real numbers on what we do for them. Tell that story everywhere it can move revenue. Measure what worked, and do more of it.

What marketing is at Whippy

Most marketers are good at one of three things. Some are great with numbers but have never sat across from a buyer. Some understand people but can't build a model. Some can tell a story but can't tell you whether it worked.

I want the person who does all three. Numbers alone are not enough, because people do not make decisions like algorithms. I learned that at the poker table: the math tells you what is right, but reading people tells you what they will actually do. A staffing owner does not buy because a spreadsheet says so. They buy because they believe it will work for them, they trust the proof, and they feel the cost of waiting. Great marketing here finds the number that matters, understands the person who has to act on it, and tells a story that makes the decision obvious.

To me, any marketing that leads to revenue is product marketing. That means:

  • ROI for staffing companies. What Whippy saves and earns a firm, in dollars and recruiter hours, and the math behind it.

  • Case studies with data. Real customers, real before and after numbers, and the story of how they decided.

  • Understanding how our customers decide. What a staffing owner, a VP of Ops, or a recruiter cares about, what they measure, and what gets them to say yes.

  • Telling the story of what we ship. We ship new products fast. Every release is a chance to get customers using more of Whippy, so it should be explained clearly and sent to the right customers to drive adoption, retention, and upsells.

If you'd be just as comfortable being screened by a hedge fund as writing a case study, keep reading.

What you will own

  1. The ROI story. Build the model of what Whippy is worth to a staffing company. Turn it into calculators, one-pagers, and talk tracks our sales team uses on live deals.

  2. Customer proof. Talk to customers, pull their numbers, and write case studies and videos that hold up when a skeptical COO checks the math.

  3. Product launches and lifecycle email. Own the changelog. Turn every release into emails that get existing customers onto new products, and track adoption and upsell, not opens.

  4. The full marketing loop. Content, then ads (Google, Meta, LinkedIn), then landing pages that capture leads, then tracking (UTMs, product events, CRM sources, attribution), then one ROI dashboard. Then use the dashboard to decide what to make next.

  5. One consistent story everywhere. Our website, trade shows, case studies, guides, changelog, and email should all sound like one company with one point of view. You own that consistency, and you work with whoever handles social so it matches too.

You will use AI to move faster and take on work that used to need more people: building pages and calculators, analyzing data, making creative, and keeping recurring work running in the background. The judgment, the customer insight, and the story are yours.

What success looks like

  • First 30 days: you have talked to our customers, learned how our buyers decide, and written down what our current marketing gets wrong

  • First 90 days: a staffing ROI model and calculator our AEs use on live deals, 2 to 3 new case studies with real numbers, and a changelog-to-email program that is driving measurable adoption and upsell

  • First six months: tracking from first click to paying customer is live, there is one dashboard of spend, leads, pipeline, and revenue by channel, and you have started testing events, paid, and AI search

  • Year one: marketing is a measurable source of pipeline and revenue, I am no longer the main person telling the Whippy story, and you can show what each channel costs and returns

How you will be measured: outcomes, not activity.

  • Qualified inbound leads per month, by channel

  • Lead-to-customer conversion rate

  • Customer acquisition cost (CAC) by channel

  • Marketing-sourced pipeline and revenue

  • Renewal and retention of marketing-sourced customers, plus upsell

  • Branded search, AI search visibility, and audience growth

How we work

Bootstrapped and profitable, so revenue is the strategy. Our customers are East Coast, so we start early. No task is above or beneath anyone here, including me, and I still cold call. We use AI to move fast, but we own our work and verify every fact. Speed over polish. Results over activity. You will always know where you stand with me.

What I'm looking for

  • You are quantitative. Funnels, unit economics, and basic stats come naturally, and you check the math before you publish the claim

  • You understand people. You can explain why a buyer said yes or no, not just what the numbers did

  • You can tell a story. You can explain a number to a busy staffing owner in one sentence, and make them care

  • You learn fast. When you hit something new, like attribution or ad bidding, you use AI as a tutor and are competent within days

  • You build instead of waiting. You make the landing page, the calculator, the deck, or the video yourself instead of filing a ticket

  • You tie everything to revenue, from first click to a paying, renewing customer

  • You have taste. AI makes it easy to produce a lot. You know which version to ship

  • Fluent written and spoken English, and able to work US Eastern hours

You do not need a marketing title or staffing experience. Finance, consulting, analytics, growth, or sales ops backgrounds are welcome. I hire the best people over the exact fit, and we will shape the role around you.

This is not for you if

  • You measure your work in impressions, likes, or opens. Here it is pipeline, revenue, and retention

  • You want a team, an agency, and a budget before you ship anything

  • You think numbers are someone else's job, or that stories are

About Whippy

Whippy is a communication, automation, and AI agent platform. You reach customers across calls, texts, and email at scale, with every conversation in one shared inbox. Replies get assigned to a teammate, handled by an AI agent, or carried forward by an automation, and the data flows back into your systems in the format you need. It cuts the repetitive work and frees teams for the human work that drives revenue.

We're industry agnostic, with our biggest wins in staffing, healthcare, and other in person businesses going through digital transformation. We're bootstrapped, profitable, and growing fast, with over 1,000 businesses using Whippy worldwide.

Whippy was founded in 2021 by me and our CTO, Jack Kennedy. Jack is an engineering machine and a marathon runner. I started BloomNation in 2011 after winning $27,205 in a poker tournament, grew it into a platform generating billions in sales for florists, then left to build something bigger with Jack.

Location

Remote, open to candidates in the United States or Latin America. We run the company on US Eastern hours, because that is when our customers are available and when our sales and CS teams are on. This role works closely with them, so you need to work those hours too. If you are somewhere else and can genuinely work East Coast hours, apply anyway. Full English fluency required.

Hiring process

  1. You apply and I review it myself

  2. A 45 minute call with me

  3. A take home: I give you a real Whippy scenario with customer data, and you come back with the numbers, the story you would tell a staffing buyer, and what you would do first. You present it to me on a 45 minute call. I check whether the math is right, whether you caught the problems in the data, and whether you used AI well and can defend your work without it

  4. A 30 minute call with Jack, our CTO

  5. References
